title: Registry isolation allowed scripts created through DOM factory aliases

reproduction.beforeFix: The registry isolation gate returned pass for dynamically created script elements, including computed tag names, aliased factories, and createElementNS.
reproduction.afterFix: The AST gate resolves createElement/createElementNS aliases and computed tag names, then rejects registry-created script elements before source admission.

rootCause: Static script checks covered source-level script tags but did not identify script elements materialized through aliased or namespace-aware DOM factory calls.
remediation: Resolve DOM factory aliases and computed tag names in the AST visitor; reject script elements produced by either document.createElement or document.createElementNS.

validation.redBeforeFix: pnpm exec vitest run packages/registry-gate/src/__tests__/registry-gate.test.ts -t "scripts created through computed and aliased DOM element factories"
validation.redBeforeFixResult: failed as expected: script elements created through direct/computed/aliased factories were accepted before the scanner change
validation.safeResourceBaseline: All 324 canonical resources pass the source-isolation matrix; none uses a script factory.

runtimeBoundary: This is a static admission-control finding for untrusted registry source. Resource code was parsed for the test and was never executed. Release-candidate deployment verification remains pending.
